\scanpage{31}
Supposons qu'il y a des territoires
constitués de blanc et noir, considérés
\unsure{indélogeables}, blanc a joué dernier
(alors c'est à noir de jouer) on a
joué $n$ coups
\[
n=p+q\qquad\deleted{\unsure{n}}n'=p'+q'\qquad n=n'
\]
\margin{$p$ : nb de pions noirs sur goban
qui ne sont prisonniers virtuels}

$q$ nb de prisonniers virtuels

$t$ territoire noir (\unsure{avec pris enlevé} les pris. bl.)

$t'$ \ldots\ blanc (\text{---} noirs)
\margin{$p+p'+t+t'=\unsure{v|\nu}^2$}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\deleted{\unsure{Q}}\ s=t+q'&\text{pts de noir potentiels}\\
s'=t'+q&\text{---}\quad\text{blanc}\quad\text{---}
\end{array}
\]
\[
d=s-s'=(t-t'\unsure{,}+(q'-q)=(t-t')+(p-p')
\]
\[
\unsure{v|\nu}^2+d=2(p+t)\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad\boxed{d=2(p+t)-\unsure{v|\nu}^2}
\]
\[
D=d\unsure{-|+}\varepsilon\qquad\varepsilon=0,1\qquad(\mathrm{NB}\quad p+t=P+T)
\]
\margin{?}
\figure{\begin{tikzpicture}\draw (0,1.8)--(0,.4)..controls (0,.15) and (.15,0)..(.3,0);\end{tikzpicture}}
Comme on ne peut prévoir la valeur de
$\varepsilon$ (est-elle indépendante de la suite du
jeu?) il est raisonnable de compenser
l'avantage de noir (de commencer)
en posant $\varepsilon=1$ (i.e. en admettant que
noir joue dernier)
\mspage{30}

doubts: The three words before les pris. bl. are not resolved securely after enlargement; do not use this phrase to infer scoring conventions.
No separate pas is visible; none is supplied.
Source punctuation is unbalanced and a small stroke follows t-prime; retained, not normalized.
observations: Second Go sheet distinguishes virtual prisoners and potential scores. Explicitly asks whether epsilon is independent of the continuation of the game, and suggests taking epsilon=1 to compensate Black’s first move. Large marginal question mark marks this reasoning. Territory-qualification wording remains uncertain.

audit.notes: Full-sheet re-reading checks virtual-prisoner wording, all primes and the unresolved epsilon sign. Board-size ambiguity made consistent with scan030. Added the visible long left bracket beside the concluding question; no missing pas supplied in the p definition.
